CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Sikka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sikka Regency.
6. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit of the Regional Government of Sikka Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and by the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Article 6
Paragraph (1)
Letter a Sufficiently clear
Letter b What is meant by establishing and implementing protection policies, programs and activities includes:
a. Collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence;
b. Providing education about anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. Conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence;
d. Conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
Letter c Sufficiently clear
Letter d Sufficiently clear
Letter e Sufficiently clear
Paragraph (2) What is meant by Regional Action Plan is the stages of programs and activities for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of acts of violence, including the worst forms of work for children, which must be carried out by SKPD in accordance with their duties and functions, prepared based on achievement targets within a period of (five) years.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear
Paragraph (4) Sufficiently clear

Article 8
The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as members of the family.

Article 3
The regulation of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is intended to provide protection and empowerment for women and children victims of violence.

Article 11
Paragraph (1)
Letter a
What is meant by complaint services is a series of actions carried out by the organizer of the integrated service institution to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and/or the community.
Letter b
What is meant by health services is efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
Letter c
Sufficiently clear.
Letter d
Sufficiently clear.
Letter e
What is meant by social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
Letter f
Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2)
Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (3)
Sufficiently clear.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 20
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
 a. guidelines and standards for fulfillment;
 b. technical guidance and training;
 c. provision of facilities;
 d. monitoring; and
 e. evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

Article 19
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted through:
   a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
   b. education and training for women victims of violence;
   c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
   d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are set forth in the form of an Agreement.

CHAPTER VI
INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government, in the context of providing protection services to women and children victims of violence, establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center.
(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children victims of violence.
(3) Further provisions regarding the Organization and Work Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 16
Letter a What is meant by the right to have one’s dignity respected is to uphold human rights.
Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d What is meant by the right to obtain information is the right to obtain information, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts, or explanations, that can be seen, heard, and read, presented in various packages and formats in accordance with developments in information and communication technology, either electronically or non-electronically, related to acts of violence.
Letter e Sufficiently clear.
Letter f What is meant by the victim’s right to social rehabilitation includes; access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, citizenship.
Letter g What is meant by the right to compensation includes; economic empowerment, return costs, health and education or skills guarantees.
Letter h What is meant by the right to complaint handling is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.
Letter i Sufficiently clear.
Letter j What is meant by the right to assistance includes, among others, psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious leaders, advocates, and family members.
What is meant by a companion is an individual who works as a volunteer to provide protection and support to women and children who are victims of acts of violence during the judicial process; companions can come from family members, friends, or independent organizations that provide attention to victims, as well as advocates.

Article 2
Letter a The principle of humanity serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children victims of acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).
Letter b The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter c The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
Letter d The principle of the best interests of victims, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and Regional Government are to fulfill the rights of women and child victims of acts of violence as regulated in laws and regulations.
Letter e Sufficiently clear

CHAPTER III
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 5
Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children victims of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Community;
c. Family; and
d. Parents.

Article 23
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to allocate budget to P2TP2A in carrying out the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) The budget allocation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be adjusted to the regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER XI
SANCTION PROVISIONS
Article 24
(1) Officials appointed to implement integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to actions and or sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations;
(2) P2TP2A managers who in carrying out the duties of protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles of implementing protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with P2TP2A internal mechanisms and sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

Article 21
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence organized by the Regional Government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent or to the DPRD.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.

24. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Sikka Regency.

6. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit of the Regional Government of Sikka Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and by the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and by the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Article 3
The regulation of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is intended to provide protection and empowerment for women and children victims of violence.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency.

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and by the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Letter a The principle of humanity serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children victims of acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).

Article 3
The regulation of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is intended to provide protection and empowerment for women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SIKKA REGENCY
NUMBER 12 OF 2012
CONCERNING
ADMINISTRATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Sikka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sikka Regency.
6. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit of the Regional Government of Sikka Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and by the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Article 23
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to allocate budget to P2TP2A in carrying out the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) The budget allocation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be adjusted to the regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Sikka Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as regulated in article 22 letter a, Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government which states that; "that in carrying out autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, oneness and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia".
On that basis, the government of Sikka Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence to respond to this while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence up to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, with adequate funding support both from the Central Government, the Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from the face of this beloved Sikka land.

Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.

22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.

24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.

26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 1

8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and by the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
